question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=(-7x)^{x}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((-7x)^{x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(-7x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(-7x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =(x)^{′}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(-7x))+(x)\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡(-7x))}^{′} \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =1\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(-7x)+x\cdot (\frac{1}{-7x}\cdot (-7)) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(-7x)+1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\operatorname{ln}⁡(-7x)+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=(-7x)^{x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =(-7x)^{x}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(-7x)+1)\end{aligned}
$$
